newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MARCH 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK GENERAL NEWS- MARCH 14.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek general press:

--Albania is facing total chaos as political parties appear unable to exert any control over developments. Unconfirmed reports say that Albanian President Sali Berisha has fled to Skopje while parties yesterday appealed to the Western European Union to send a force to restore order.

--The government is hoping to marry public and private interests in a new telecoms organisation, expected to operate as an alternate to state-run OTE. The issue was broached by Development Minister Vasso Papandreou at her meeting yesterday with leading Greek entrepreneurs.

--Further restraints on state spending will be the government's first response to the slackening of tax revenues noted recently. According to the finance ministry, new measures have not been ruled out.
--Greece is ready to participate in any international peace forece if it is decided: preparations to evacuate Greek citizens are under way.
--Greek investors, however, are preparing for better days in the Balkans with, conferring with the development minister yesterday on possible investments in neighbouring countries.
--Greek frigate Egeon is sailing towards the port of Dyrahio in the event of the need to evacuate Greeks: Unconfirmed reports say Athens is prepared to offer asylum to Berisha if he requests it.

--Education Minister Gerasimos Arsenis and Prime Minister Costas Simitis yesterday discussed the probability of employing teachers on a casual basis to replace teachers on the eighth week of their strike.
--Compensation for tenants evicted from business premises will rise, in some cases, to double previous amounts, in line with a new amendment. --Maria Petrakis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
